description: Hashable primitives providing bounded, deterministic hash codes suitable for bucket-based collections. Z3 verifies post-condition bounds (result >= 0 and result < num_buckets for the bucket step), closing the gap left by prelude.mm which only defines Eq/Ord. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/hash — verified hashable primitives'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/core.mm and std/contracts.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/contracts.mm already use (checked_add, checked_mul, safe_narrow, abs_val, modulo, conditional expressions).

atoms.name: hash_bucket
atoms.description: Map a non-negative hash code into a bucket index in [0, num_buckets) using modulo. This is the fundamental post-hashing step every open-addressing or chaining container needs.

atoms.name: hash_combine
atoms.description: Combine two hash codes into a single hash code using a bounded linear mix. Keeps the result within a safe range so that downstream hash_bucket has a non-negative input.

atoms.name: hash_i64_nonneg
atoms.description: Deterministic hash of a non-negative i64 clamped into [0, max_hash]. Acts as the default Hashable implementation for sized integer keys.

atoms.name: hash_eq_consistent
atoms.description: Encoded Hashable law check: when the two inputs are equal the result MUST be 1 (hash_eq_consistent(x, x) == 1). Z3 proves the law by evaluating the equality predicate directly. This atom is the machine-checkable witness that `eq(a, b) => hash(a) == hash(b)` holds for the numeric hashes exposed by this module.
